fullPassage: Resilience: The Power to Overcome City Wellness Center Newsletter This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events. There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. Proceed with what you were doing. Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected. Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors. Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength. Good communication helps resilience. This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks. I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty. Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger. However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.

questions.passage: ” Athlete Aimee Mullins also ①<u>saw</u> her challenges as an opportunity.  She ②<u>were born</u> with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery.  She ③<u>competed</u> against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996.  Her career also ④<u>includes</u> modeling, acting, and public speaking.  She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② were born → was born: 주어가 She(그녀, 한 명=단수)라서 be동사의 과거형은 was를 써요. were는 복수(we, they 등)에 쓰는 형태라 여기엔 안 맞아요
det.analysis:
① saw: 'Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity'는 '운동선수 Aimee Mullins도 자신의 시련을 기회로 여겼다'예요. 과거의 일이라 see의 과거형 saw가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② were born → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'She were born with a medical condition'은 '그녀는 어떤 병을 가지고 태어났다'예요. 주어가 She, 즉 한 사람(단수)이에요. be동사의 과거형은 단수 주어에는 was, 복수 주어에는 were를 써요. 그래서 were born이 아니라 was born으로 고쳐야 해요. ❌ were born은 틀림 ←정답

③ competed: 'She competed against athletes without disabilities'는 '그녀는 비장애인 선수들과 겨루었다'예요. 과거의 일이라 compete의 과거형 competed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ includes: 'Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking'는 '그녀의 경력에는 모델 활동, 연기, 강연도 포함된다'예요. 주어 Her career(그녀의 경력)가 단수라 동사에 -s를 붙인 includes가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 주어가 She(한 명=단수)면 be동사 과거는 was. were는 복수용

questions.passage: If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and ①<u>grow</u> from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.  There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but ②<u>using it</u> as a stepping stone to growth.  Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected ③<u>were</u> the sources for his most popular stories.  “The hardship was a real blessing that ④<u>inspired</u> me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② using it → used it: 'not only survived ... but used ...'는 'not only A but (also) B'라는 짝 표현으로, survived(과거)와 형태를 맞춰 used(과거)를 써야 해요
det.analysis:
① grow: 'Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity'는 '더 나아가, 여러분은 역경으로부터 배우고 성장한다'예요. 주어 you에 어울리는 원형 grow가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② using it → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 원문은 'people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone'(역경을 견뎌냈을 뿐 아니라 그것을 성장의 발판으로 삼은 사람들)이에요. 'not only A but (also) B'는 A와 B의 형태를 똑같이 맞춰야 하는 짝 표현이에요. 앞이 survived(과거동사)니까 뒤도 과거동사 used로 맞춰야 해요. 그래서 -ing형 using이 아니라 used로 써야 해요. ❌ using it은 틀림 ←정답

③ were: 'his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience ... were the sources'는 '어린 시절의 가난, 아버지를 일찍 여읜 것, 그리고 ... 경험이 (그의) 원천이었다'예요. 주어가 A, B, and C 세 가지(복수)라 were가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ inspired: 'a real blessing that inspired me to write stories'는 '내가 이야기를 쓰도록 영감을 준 진정한 축복'이에요. 관계사 that의 동사로 과거형 inspired가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: not only A but (also) B → A와 B 형태 일치. survived(과거)면 used(과거)

questions.passage: If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and ①<u>benefit</u> from difficult life events. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of ③<u>been disrespected</u> were the sources for his most popular stories.  “The ④<u>hardship</u> was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ been disrespected → being disrespected: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써야 해요. '무시당하는 것'이라는 수동의 뜻이라 being + 과거분사(being disrespected) 형태가 맞아요
det.analysis:
① benefit: 'the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events'는 '어려운 인생의 일들을 감당하고, 회복하고, 거기서 이득을 얻는 능력'이에요. to handle / recover / benefit이 나란히 이어지는 자리라 원형 benefit이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② survived: 'people who not only survived adversity'는 '역경을 견뎌낸 사람들'이에요. 관계사 who의 동사로 과거형 survived가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ been disrespected → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 원문은 'his experience of being disrespected'(무시당한 경험)이에요. 밑줄 앞에 전치사 of가 있어요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 그냥 쓸 수 없고 동명사(-ing) 형태로 바꿔야 해요. 게다가 '무시하는' 게 아니라 '무시당하는' 수동의 뜻이라 'being + 과거분사'인 being disrespected가 맞아요. been disrespected는 앞에 have가 있어야 쓰는 형태라 여기엔 안 맞아요. ❌ been disrespected는 틀림 ←정답

④ hardship: '“The hardship was a real blessing'은 '그 고난은 진정한 축복이었다'예요. 문장의 주어로 명사 hardship이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤 = 동명사. '~당하는'(수동)이면 being + 과거분사 → being disrespected

questions.passage: Good ①<u>communication</u> helps resilience.  This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good ②<u>support</u> networks.  I am not saying that these strategies are ③<u>hard</u> or remove all stress and suffering.  Still, I ④<u>urge</u> you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ hard → easy: 바로 뒤에서 '이 전략들을 꾸준히 실천하라'고 권하는 흐름이라, 저자는 '이 전략들이 쉽다고 말하는 건 아니다'라고 해야 앞뒤가 맞아요. 그래서 easy(쉬운)가 맞아요
det.analysis:
① communication: 'Good communication helps resilience'는 '좋은 의사소통은 회복력에 도움이 된다'예요. 남과 대화하고 도움을 주고받는 흐름이라 '의사소통(communication)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② support: 'resilient people tend to create good support networks'는 '회복력이 강한 사람들은 좋은 지지망을 만드는 경향이 있다'예요. 서로 돕는 사람들의 관계망이라 '지지(support)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ hard → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'I am not saying that these strategies are easy'(나는 이 전략들이 쉽다고 말하는 것은 아니다)예요. 바로 뒤에서 '그래도 꾸준히 실천하라'고 권해요. 즉 '쉽지는 않지만 그래도 하라'는 흐름이라 easy(쉬운)가 맞아요. hard(어려운)로 바꾸면 '어렵다고 말하는 건 아니다'가 되어 뒤 문장과 어긋나요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

④ urge: 'I urge you to practice them whenever you can'은 '나는 여러분이 할 수 있을 때마다 그것들을 실천하기를 강력히 권한다'예요. 실천을 권유하는 상황이라 '강력히 권하다(urge)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: '쉽다고 말하는 건 아니지만 그래도 실천하라'는 흐름 → easy(쉬운). hard는 반대

questions.passage: Here are three basic ①<u>strategies</u> to build up this “resilience muscle. ” Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience Muscle” First, accept and respect adversity as a ②<u>unnatural</u> part of life.  This doesn’t mean being passive, but ③<u>understanding</u> that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress.  Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t.  Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you ④<u>confront</u> them as a learning process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② unnatural → natural: 역경을 '삶의 자연스러운 일부'로 받아들이라는 조언이라 natural(자연스러운)이 맞아요. unnatural(부자연스러운)은 정반대예요
det.analysis:
① strategies: 'Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.”'는 '이 “회복력 근육”을 키우는 세 가지 기본 전략이 여기 있다'예요. 뒤에 방법을 소개하는 글이라 '전략(strategies)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② unnatural → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life'(역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고 존중하라)예요. 역경은 누구에게나 일어나는 삶의 당연한 부분이라는 뜻이라 natural(자연스러운)이 맞아요. unnatural(부자연스러운, 이상한)로 바꾸면 '역경은 삶의 이상한 부분'이 되어 '받아들이고 존중하라'는 조언과 어긋나요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ understanding: 'This doesn't mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress'는 '이것은 수동적이 되라는 뜻이 아니라, 삶의 어떤 변화가 고통이나 스트레스를 줄 수 있음을 이해하라는 뜻이다'예요. 받아들임의 참뜻을 설명하는 자리라 '이해하는 것(understanding)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ confront: 'help you confront them as a learning process'는 '그것들을 배움의 과정으로 마주하도록 돕는다'예요. 도전과 시련을 피하지 않고 마주하라는 흐름이라 '마주하다(confront)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 역경을 삶의 당연한 일부로 받아들이라 → natural(자연스러운). unnatural은 반대

questions.passage: Third, be connected.  Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors.  Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and __________.  Good communication helps resilience.  This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① respond to it with more strength(더 큰 힘으로 그것에 대응하다): 남과 고민을 나누면 상황을 더 명확히 보게 되고, 그래서 더 강하게 대처할 수 있다는 흐름이에요
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Talking about your issues with someone can help you see your situation with more clarity and ___'(누군가와 고민을 이야기하면 상황을 더 명확하게 보고 ___ 데 도움이 될 수 있다). 앞에서 '더 명확하게 본다(more clarity)'고 했고, 바로 뒤 문장에서 'Good communication helps resilience(좋은 의사소통은 회복력에 도움이 된다)'라고 해요. 즉 대화의 좋은 효과를 이어서 말하는 자리예요.

✅ ① respond to it with more strength(더 큰 힘으로 그것에 대응하다): 상황을 명확히 보고, 그 상황에 더 강하게 대처한다는 긍정적 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② ignore it completely(그것을 완전히 무시하다): 대화로 도움을 얻는 흐름과 반대예요.

❌ ③ forget about your problems(네 문제를 잊어버리다): 문제를 직시해 대처한다는 취지와 어긋나요.

❌ ④ blame others for it(그것을 남 탓하다): 본문에 없는 부정적 태도라 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: 대화 → 상황을 명확히 봄 + 더 강하게 대처(respond with more strength)

ch: respond to it with more strength

questions.passage: To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience.  Resilience means springing back, just like __________ after hitting the ground.  If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ a bouncy ball(잘 튀는 공): 회복력은 '튀어 오르는 것'이라 했고, 땅에 부딪힌 뒤 다시 튀어 오르는 것은 잘 튀는 공이에요
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Resilience means springing back, just like ___ after hitting the ground'(회복력이란 땅에 부딪힌 뒤 ___처럼 다시 튀어 오르는 것을 의미한다). 핵심은 '튀어 오른다(springing back)'예요. 바로 뒤 문장에서도 'you can bounce back and recover quickly(다시 튀어 올라 빠르게 회복할 수 있다)'라고 이어져요.

❌ ① a falling rock(떨어지는 바위): 바위는 떨어지기만 하고 튀어 오르지 않아요.

❌ ② a melting ice cube(녹는 얼음 조각): 녹아 없어지는 것이라 '튀어 오름'과 무관해요.

✅ ③ a bouncy ball(잘 튀는 공): 땅에 부딪힌 뒤 다시 튀어 오르는 대표적인 예라 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ a broken glass(깨진 유리): 깨져 버리는 것이라 다시 튀어 오르는 회복력의 비유와 반대예요.
det.tip: springing back(튀어 오름) + 땅에 부딪힌 뒤 다시 튐 → 잘 튀는 공(a bouncy ball)

questions.passage: ” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity.  She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery.  She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996.  Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking.  She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 'Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking'과 일치해요. 그녀의 경력에는 모델·연기·강연이 포함돼요
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs'로, 교통사고가 아니라 '타고난 의학적 질환' 때문에 두 다리를 잃었어요. '교통사고'는 사실과 달라요.

questions.passage: If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience.  Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity.  So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.  There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth.  Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories.  “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling. ” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity.  She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① how people recover from and grow through adversity(사람들이 역경에서 회복하고 성장하는 방법)
det.analysis:
글은 역경에서 다시 튀어 올라 회복하고(bounce back), 나아가 배우고 성장한다는 회복력을 설명하고, 그 예로 동화 작가 Andersen과 운동선수 Aimee Mullins가 고난을 성공의 발판으로 삼은 이야기를 들어요.

✅ ① how people recover from and grow through adversity(사람들이 역경에서 회복하고 성장하는 방법): 글 전체를 아우르는 핵심이라 정답이에요. ←정답

❌ ② why old fairy tales still appeal to modern readers(옛 동화가 오늘날 독자에게도 사랑받는 이유): Andersen은 예시일 뿐, 동화의 인기 이유를 다루지 않아요.

❌ ③ the daily training routines of famous athletes(유명 운동선수들의 하루 훈련 일과): 훈련 방법을 다루는 글이 아니에요.

❌ ④ the long history of the modern Paralympic Games(현대 패럴림픽의 오랜 역사): 패럴림픽은 잠깐 언급될 뿐, 그 역사를 다루지 않아요.
det.tip: 역경 → 회복하고(bounce back) + 배우고 성장(grow) = 글의 핵심

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"어떤 삶도 문제로부터 자유롭지 않다." (6단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) free, from, is, life, No, problems 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: No life is free from problems
det.analysis:
문장의 주어는 'No life(어떤 삶도 ~않다)'예요. 명사 앞에 No를 붙이면 '어떤 ~도 …않다'라는 전체 부정이 돼서, No life가 문장 맨 앞 주어 자리에 와요.

동사는 be동사 is예요. 주어 life가 단수라 is를 써요.

'~로부터 자유롭다'는 be free from ~이라는 굳어진 표현(연어)이에요. free 뒤에 반드시 전치사 from이 붙고, 그 뒤에 대상이 와요. 그래서 is free from 순서가 고정돼요.

마지막으로 '문제'는 problems를 써서 from 뒤에 놓아요.

순서대로 이으면 No / life / is / free / from / problems. 'be free from' 연어와 'No + 명사' 주어 구조 때문에 이 순서 하나로만 배열돼요.
det.tip: '~로부터 자유롭다' = be free from ~ (free 뒤 from 고정) / 'No + 명사' = 어떤 ~도 …않다

questions.wa: No life is free from problems

questions.passage: Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself.  Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor ①<u>worry</u> about the future.  Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise.  If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique.  It works like this.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: worry → worrying: 'neither A nor B(A도 B도 아닌)'는 A와 B의 형태를 맞춰야 해요. 앞이 regretting(-ing형)이라 뒤도 worrying(-ing형)으로 써야 해요
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor ①worry about the future'예요. '과거를 후회하지도, 미래를 걱정하지도 않으면서 현재 순간에 머물라'는 뜻이에요.

'neither A nor B'는 'A도 B도 아닌'이라는 짝 표현이에요. 이때 A와 B는 형태가 똑같아야 해요. 여기서 A 자리에는 regretting(후회하는 것)이라는 -ing형이 왔어요. 그러니 B 자리도 똑같이 -ing형으로 맞춰야 해요.

그래서 원형 worry가 아니라 regretting과 짝이 되는 worrying으로 고쳐야 해요.

따라서 worry를 worrying으로 바꿔 씁니다.
det.tip: neither A nor B → 형태 일치. regretting(-ing)이면 worrying(-ing)

questions.passage: This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress.  Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me? ”, you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t.  Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process.  __________!
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"역경 없이는 결코 일어날 수 없었을 그 모든 성공담을 떠올려 보라." (13단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) adversity, all, could, happened, have, never, of, stories, success, that, the, Think, without 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 13단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity
det.analysis:
'~을 떠올려 보라'는 명령문이라 동사원형 Think로 시작해요. '~을 생각하다/떠올리다'는 think of이므로 Think of로 이어요.

무엇을 떠올리는가 하면 'all the success stories(그 모든 성공담)'예요. all → the → success → stories 순서로 놓아요.

그다음 '역경 없이는 결코 일어날 수 없었을'은 앞의 stories를 꾸며 주는 관계사절이라 that으로 이어요.

'결코 일어날 수 없었을'은 could never have happened로 써요. 이것은 'could have p.p.(~했을 수도 있었다)'에 부정의 never를 넣어 '결코 ~할 수 없었을 것이다'라는 과거의 가정을 나타내요.

마지막으로 '역경 없이는'은 without adversity예요.

순서대로 이으면 Think / of / all / the / success / stories / that / could / never / have / happened / without / adversity.
det.tip: '결코 ~할 수 없었을 것이다' = could never have + 과거분사(happened)

questions.wa: Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity
accept: Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity

questions.passage: Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger.  However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges.  Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones.  Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges.  So, building resilience is the key __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (앞의 the key에 이어지는 부분)
"(회복력을 기르는 것은) 역경을 극복하는 것뿐만 아니라 행복한 삶을 사는 것에도 (열쇠이다)."

[ a / adversity / also / but / happy / life / living / not / only / overcoming / to / to ] (12단어) (영어로)

det.korean: not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life
det.analysis:
핵심 뼈대는 'not only A but also B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)'라는 짝 표현이에요. 이 틀은 순서가 고정돼서 not → only → (A) → but → also → (B)로만 배열돼요.

앞에 the key가 있고, 'the key to ~(~의 열쇠)'라서 A와 B 앞에 각각 전치사 to가 필요해요. 그래서 to가 두 번 쓰여요.

A(역경을 극복하는 것)는 to overcoming adversity예요. 전치사 to 뒤라 동명사 overcoming을 쓰고, 목적어 adversity를 붙여요.

B(행복한 삶을 사는 것)는 to living a happy life예요. 역시 to 뒤에 동명사 living, 그 뒤에 목적어 a happy life(a → happy → life)를 놓아요.

순서대로 이으면 not / only / to / overcoming / adversity / but / also / to / living / a / happy / life. 'not only ~ but also' 틀과 우리말이 A(극복)를 먼저 지정하므로 배열은 이 하나로 강제돼요.
det.tip: 'A뿐만 아니라 B도' = not only A but also B (틀 고정) / 'the key to + 동명사'라 to가 두 번

questions.wa: not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life
accept: not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life

questions.passage: Stop whatever you are doing.  Take a few deep breaths.  Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad.  __________.  Or start something different based on what you observed.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"네가 하던 일을 계속하라." (6단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) doing, Proceed, were, what, with, you 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Proceed with what you were doing
det.analysis:
'계속하라'는 명령문이라 동사원형 Proceed로 시작해요. proceed는 '계속 진행하다'라는 뜻인데, '~을 계속하다'라고 대상을 말할 때는 'proceed with ~'처럼 전치사 with를 붙여요. 그래서 Proceed with 순서가 고정돼요.

'네가 하던 일'은 명사절 what you were doing으로 나타내요. 여기서 what은 '~하는 것'이라는 뜻이고, 명사절 안에서는 의문문 어순이 아니라 'what + 주어(you) + 동사(were doing)'의 평서문 어순을 써요. 그래서 what you were doing 순서가 고정돼요.

이 명사절 전체가 with의 목적어가 돼요.

순서대로 이으면 Proceed / with / what / you / were / doing. 'proceed with' 연어와 명사절 어순 때문에 배열이 이 하나로만 정해져요.
det.tip: '~을 계속하다' = proceed with ~ / 명사절은 'what + 주어 + 동사'(의문문 어순 아님)

questions.wa: Proceed with what you were doing
accept: Proceed with what you were doing
